bridgeRegions.note: Dictionary wrapper selection; non-BRIDGE uses a real locking/concurrent implementation. Java: ConcurrentHashMap or synchronized map.
Non-BRIDGE supports \UXXXXXXXX escapes producing surrogate pairs. Java must implement via Character.toChars / appendCodePoint; invalid code points throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException in C# (trap).
BRIDGE uses a stub cancellation; non-BRIDGE uses CancellationToken. Java: mirror with a small CancellationToken class or volatile flag.
Non-BRIDGE falls back to culture-sensitive .NET TimeSpan.TryParse before 'min'/'max' handling. Java needs a hand-written TimeSpan.TryParse equivalent (format [-][d.]hh:mm:ss[.fffffff]); culture trap.
BRIDGE uses non-atomic fallbacks (JS single-threaded); non-BRIDGE uses System.Threading.Interlocked. Java: AtomicReference / VarHandle.
Comment only: '// keep line for BRIDGE.NET bug' - no conditional code.
Comment only: blank-line-before-#endregion workaround for Bridge.NET crash - no conditional code.

notes: Generated sources are NOT committed upstream (git-ignored); the only checked-in inputs are SyntaxNodeInfos.cs and *CommandInfos.cs. Java port needs a Java reimplementation of SyntaxNodeGenerator run at build time (recommended) or a one-time generated and committed set of Java files.
Namespace discrepancy: SyntaxNodeGenerator/CodeGenerator/SyntaxNodeInfos use Kusto.Language.Generator (singular); CommandGenerator/Grammar/CommandInfo/*CommandInfos use Kusto.Language.Generators.
Generators' .cs files are dual-use: wrapped in '// <#+ ... // #>' so T4 can include them as class-feature blocks; under #if !T4 they are ordinary C#. Do not mirror the T4 wrapper in Java.

Generated node classes are partial; hand-written halves live in Kusto.Language/Syntax/*.cs. Java mirror rule (partials merge into one file) conflicts with generation; recommend generator emitting the generated members into the merged file via marker regions, or emitting an abstract *Base class per node.
Generated syntax nodes reference Kusto.Language.Editor.CompletionKind/CompletionHint (GetCompletionHintCore); these two enums must be ported (or stubbed) even though Editor is out of scope.
Non-BRIDGE (full .NET) branches are the reference behaviour for the Java port.
